Set-up

Download the w5-regression-analysis. This folder contains the R script template and datasets to be used for this workshop.
Install the modelsummary package if you haven’t done so already.
Load the required packages: tidyverse, haven, readxl, janitor, gtsummary, report, and modelsummary.



1. Simple Linear Regression

Import the dataset pie_sales.xlsx and clean the column names.

Run a descriptive analysis of the variables.

Generate a quick data summary using the datasummary_skim() function.

Regress pie sales on price and advertising costs.

Run the summary of the regression model.

Use the modelsummary package to generate a regression table.



2. Multiple Linear Regression

Import the dataset prod_cacao.xlsx.

Run descriptive statistics and a quick data summary.

Specify a regression function for peak harvest using inputs: seedling, labor, fertilizer, organic inputs, and herbicide/others.

Estimate the regression model and run the summary.

Generate a model summary table using modelsummary.

Use the report package to generate an interpretation of the regression results.



3. Logistic Regression

Import the dataset adoption.xlsx.

Run descriptive statistics and a quick data summary for the adoption variables.

Fit a logistic regression model with adoption as the dependent variable and predictors: age, education, and cage area.

Run the summary of the logistic regression model.

Generate a regression table using modelsummary.

Use the report package to generate an interpretation of the logistic regression results.

Set-up

Using the R project folder serdac-r-workshop, create a new folder named w3-data-viz. Download the w3-data-viz-exercise-template.R file and save it in the w3-data-viz folder.
Install the tidyverse, babynames, and tidyplots package if you haven’t done so already.



1. Line Plot

Using the US baby names dataset from the babynames package, select at least 3 baby names with the same gender.

Create a line plot showing how the popularity (number of babies given each name) changes over time.

Save the plot as an image file.



2. Scatter Plot

Create a scatter plot using the eu_countries dataset from the tidyplots package.

Plot country area against population.

Add vertical and horizontal reference lines to highlight thresholds.

Save the plot as an image file.



3. Stacked Bar Plot

Using the energy dataset, create a stacked bar plot of energy sources across years (2008 onwards).

Show the relative contribution of each energy source per year using normalized bars.

Save the plot as an image file.



4. Box Plot

Using the study dataset, create a boxplot with treatment on the x-axis and score on the y-axis.

Include error bars, individual data points, and a minimal theme.

Save the plot as an image file.



5. Bar Plot

Create a bar plot of study scores grouped by treatment.

Add mean bars with standard error bars.

Overlay individual data points and include test asterisks to indicate statistical significance.

Save the plot as an image file.



6. Area Stack

Using the energy_week dataset, create an area stack plot of power across dates.

Show how total power output changes over time, broken down by energy source.

Save the plot as an image file.

1. R and RStudio Installation
1.1. Install R and RStudio on your computer.
1.2. Download the entire R project folder serdac-r-workshop from the provided Google Drive link. Save the folder on your computer. This folder will serve as our working directory for the entire duration of the training.
1.3. Inside the serdac-r-workshop folder, navigate to w1-getting-started-r. This folder contains the R script template and the datasets to be used for this workshop.


2. R Packages
2.1. Install the following R packages:

tidyverse
readxl
haven
janitor

2.2. Load the installed packages using the library() function.


3. Importing Data
3.1. Use the functions glimpse(), View(), and summary() to check the structure and contents of the imported datasets.
3.2. Load the file swimming_pools.csv and the file potatoes.csv using both read_csv() and read.csv(). Compare the differences in the outputs.
3.3. Load the Excel file urban_pop.xls using read_xls() or read_excel().
3.4. Load the SPSS file HBAT.sav using read_sav().
3.5. Load the online Stata dataset from http://www.stata-press.com/data/r9/auto.dta and save it into a variable named auto.

text:
Set-up

Using the R project folder serdac-r-workshop, navigate to w2-data-wrangling. This folder contains the R script template to be used for this workshop.
Install the tidyverse and gapminder packages if you haven’t done so already.
Load the packages using the library() function.



1. Basic Data Wrangling with Tidyverse

Use the gapminder dataset from the gapminder package.

Check the data using the glimpse() and View() functions.



1.1. filter()

Using the gapminder dataset, filter the data for the year 1957.

Filter for Philippines in 2002.

Filter for the year 1957, then arrange in descending order of population.



1.2. mutate()

Use mutate() to compute GDP (gdpPercap * pop).

Filter for year 2007, compute GDP in millions, and arrange data by descending life expectancy.



1.3. group_by() and summarize()

Summarize to find the median life expectancy per country and arrange in descending order.

Find median life expectancy and maximum GDP per capita in each year.



2. Import the dataset s2-sample-data.xlsx

Save the first sheet as fct_items and use the clean_names() function from janitor package to clean the column names.
Using pivot_longer(), reshape the factor items (ci_1 to ewb_10) into long format. Label the names as item and the values as value. Save the data as fct_items_long_fmt



3. Import the dataset s2-sample-data.xlsx again, this time using the second sheet

Save the second sheet as fct_label
Using left_join(), merge the two datasets (e.g., fct_items_long_fmt, fct_label)



BONUS: Sample Visualization with Gapminder

Run the provided code snippet and observe the output.


gapminder |> 
  filter(year == 2007) |>  
  ggplot(aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp, color = continent, size = pop)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_size(range = c(0.1, 20), name = "Population") +
  labs(x = "GDP per Capita",
       y = "Life Expectancy (years)",
       title = "World Development in 2007") +
  theme_light() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
